drafted_from: tool row in tools/track-and-compare-movement/tool-rows.json, do-work/track_selected_object.py and test/test_track_selected_object.py (the refusal was run; the model run is read from the code and test)
start_here: Say to your AI: "In /work/square.mp4 follow the white square I pointed at one second in (a point at 34% across and 50% down), for seconds 0 to 3, and write the outline for every frame to /work/square-mask." It reads the tool's row and runs track_selected_object.py on your computer with a SAM 2 video model.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads video or pose files on the person's own computer and writes a new file or folder beside them.
instructions: 1. Choose the clip, the stretch (up to 30 seconds) and the second you pointed at; get a frame at that second and turn the point you chose into x and y between 0 and 1, adding a point outside the object (include false) if something similar sits next to it.

2. Have the model ready once beforehand: the script runs offline from the local Hugging Face cache (for example facebook/sam2.1-hiera-tiny) with ffmpeg, numpy, pillow, torch and transformers installed.
3. The AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: tool:track-a-selected-object-in-a-video} and runs its `run` command with an output folder that does not exist yet.

4. Read the last line: {"result": {start, end, fps, frames, width, height, selected_frame, pixels, model}} or {"error": ...}; the folder holds mask.mkv, a mask and a transparent preview picture per frame, and result.json. A frame with an empty mask (pixels 0) means the object was hidden.

worked_examples.title: Follow a white square for three seconds
worked_examples.ask: In /work/square.mp4 follow the white square I pointed at one second in, for seconds 0 to 3.
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/track-and-compare-movement/do-work/track_selected_object.py and the real-model case of test/test_track_selected_object.py (not run here: it needs the SAM 2 model in the local cache). The video is 320x240 at 12 frames a second, a black picture with a 60 by 60 white square moving right from x 20 to 200. Command: motion-env/bin/python tools/track-and-compare-movement/do-work/track_selected_object.py --video /work/square.mp4 --output /work/square-mask --start 0 --end 3 --time 1 --points '[{"x":0.34375,"y":0.5,"include":true},{"x":0.9,"y":0.1,"include":false}]' --fps 12 --model facebook/sam2.1-hiera-tiny --device cpu.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result": {"start": 0.0, "end": 3.0, "fps": 12, "frames": 36, "width": 720, "height": 540, "selected_frame": 12, "pixels": [36 counts, one per frame], "model": "facebook/sam2.1-hiera-tiny"}} Frames are scaled to fit 720 by 720, so 320x240 becomes 720x540 and the square is 3600*(720/320)^2 = 18225 pixels; the test needs pixels[12] between 14580 and 23692 and more than 24 frames above half that area. /work/square-mask then holds mask.mkv, masks/00000.png to 00035.png, preview/ and result.json.

worked_examples.title: A stretch over 30 seconds is refused before anything is made
worked_examples.ask: Follow the square for seconds 0 to 45.
worked_examples.given: I ran this refusal with python3 -I tools/track-and-compare-movement/do-work/track_selected_object.py --video /work/square.mp4 --output /work/never-made --start 0 --end 45 --time 1 --points '[{"x":0.34,"y":0.5,"include":true}]' --fps 12 --model facebook/sam2.1-hiera-tiny; it exits 2 and the output folder is not created (test_a_range_over_thirty_seconds).
worked_examples.hands_back: {"error": "Choose a mask range up to 30 seconds containing the selected frame."}
